title: Cloudflare, 2 July 2019 — a regex ate every CPU
what: A WAF rule with catastrophic regex backtracking was deployed globally; every edge machine went to 100% CPU and served 502s for 27 minutes.

steps.note: WAF rule deployed: each request now costs ~30× the CPU at the edge

timeline.text: The rule deploys to the whole edge at once
First alerts: synthetic WAF test failures, traffic dropping
“We had lost 80% of our traffic” — WAF identified
Global WAF kill switch executed
Traffic and CPU back to normal

sources.label: Cloudflare: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019

assumptions: Your edge services take the role of Cloudflare’s WAF: their CPU cost per request rises ~30×, so capacity drops to ~3% for 25 minutes (deploy → kill switch).
Only CPU-bound edge capacity is cut; downstream services keep theirs.

title: GitHub, 21 October 2018 — 43 seconds, 24 hours
what: A 43-second network partition made the database orchestrator promote West-coast MySQL primaries; East-coast apps then wrote across the country for most of a day.

steps.note: 43 s partition between the US-East hub and data center
Primaries promoted in US West: every database call crosses the country (~60 ms)

timeline.text: Optical equipment maintenance cuts US-East hub ↔ data center for 43 s
Orchestrator promotes US-West database primaries
Deploys locked; status yellow
Status red; apps in US-East now write to US-West
Back to green Oct 22 23:03 UTC after 5M webhook events were drained

assumptions: Your primary database plays GitHub’s MySQL primaries: 43 s unreachable, then ~60 ms extra on every call (US coast-to-coast round trip) for the rest of the window.
Requests that call the database several times pay the 60 ms each time.
The first six hours of the 24-hour incident are replayed, at 70–80% of your usual load (Sunday evening).

title: Slack, 4 January 2021 — the Monday after the holidays
what: Cold client caches pulled data all at once on the first workday of the year; AWS Transit Gateways saturated, packets dropped, and autoscaling tried to add 1,200 servers while provisioning itself was failing.

steps.note: Packet loss creeping up between services
Transit Gateway saturated: retransmits and dropped calls everywhere
Provisioning fails: open-file limit and AWS quota hit while 1,200 servers were requested

timeline.text: Only 99% of messages sending successfully
Mini-peak plus degraded network saturates the web tier; Slack unavailable
Autoscaling asks for 1,200 more web servers
Provisioning service recovers
Web tier has enough capacity; still degraded
AWS raises Transit Gateway capacity; network normal

sources.label: Slack Engineering: Slack’s outage on January 4th 2021

assumptions: Traffic: your morning ramp, then 1.55× your usual peak at 07:00 while cold caches refill (Slack gave no number; this is the assumption to tune).
Network loss is applied to every component: 1.5% of calls fail and 40 ms is added while the gateways are saturated.
Your autoscaled services cannot launch anything for 74 minutes, then launch 4× slower for an hour.

title: AWS us-east-1, 20 October 2025 — DynamoDB lost its DNS
what: A race in DynamoDB’s DNS automation emptied the regional endpoint record. Everything that depended on DynamoDB failed, including EC2’s own instance-launch system, which then took hours to recover.

steps.note: EC2 cannot launch instances (droplet leases expired, then congestive collapse)
Launches resume; network configuration propagates slowly
NLB health checks flap on instances without network config
Health-check failover disabled; residual connection errors

timeline.text: DynamoDB endpoint stops resolving; EC2 launch leases start timing out
DNS identified as the source
DNS records restored
EC2 work throttled, DWFM hosts restarted
Instance launches possible again
NLB connection errors from flapping health checks
All EC2 launches normal

sources.label: AWS: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB service disruption in us-east-1

assumptions: Your managed key-value store (or your primary database, if you have none) is unreachable for 2 h 37 min — assumes it lives in us-east-1.
Your autoscaled services cannot add capacity until 05:28, then launch 4× slower until 13:50.
Your edge sees load-balancer connection errors: 2% until 09:36, then 0.4% until 14:09.
